newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the Midwestern U.S. were steady to higher Friday with continued electricity constraints out of central Canada, industry sources said.

Traders said purchasing electricity from the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) was difficult with the Canadian transmission constraints, while Manitoba Hydro expected the problem to be repaired this weekend, the sources said.

In the East Central Area Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Saturday were pegged at $14.50-15.50, while Sunday was assessed at $13.50-14.50 and Monday at $18.00-19.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Next-day ECAR was talked near $17.00 on Thursday.
Peak electricity for the five business days of next week were assessed at $17.00-19.50 per MWh.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was talked steady in the $12.50-14.00 area, the sources said.
November ECAR prices held at $17.25-17.55, while December was said near $18.70-19.10. January/February ECAR business was assessed steady at $20.85-21.00 per MWh.

Peak, non-firm power prices for Saturday delivery in the MAPP region were talked at $13.50-14.50, while Sunday was assessed at $13.00-14.00 and Monday was steady from Friday delivery prices at $15.00-16.00 per MWh.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power was assessed also steady at $8.00-10.00.

In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN), non-firm peak power for Saturday delviery was said to be at $14.00-15.00, while Sunday was seen at $12.50-13.50 and Monday near $18.00 from a Friday delivery range at $16.50-18.00, the sources said.
Off-peak next day power was pegged steady in the $11.50-13.00 range.
Peak MAIN power for the five business days of next week were seen at $16.00-17.00 per MWh.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak, non-firm power for Saturday delivery was assessed at $18.50-19.50 and Monday was pegged at $19.00-20.00 for the entire region.
Next day SPP power was assessed at $18.50-22.50 on Thursday.
Off-peak prices in SPP held steady in the $12.00-14.00 area, the sources said.
November SPP was discussed steady near $18.50 in the north and $19.25 in the south, while December SPP was talked in the $22.25-22.50 range for the south region, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
